main_text.p: tur, Synecdochicè signo tribuit: signi vero nominatim facit mentionem, non quod virtutem aliquam compescendi magica illi putauerit inesse, sed partim vt ceremonia illa significarent à Christo crucifixo quem inuocabant virtute illam proficisci, partim vt quem oratione, eundem & gestu, signoq; ordinario profiterentur.
Basilius lib. de Spiritu S. cap. 27. inter primas traditiones Apostolicas ponit signare se signo crucis.

Resp. I. Constat Basilium nimium interdum fuisse traditionibus addictū. Praeter signationem crucis, etiā inter Apostolicas traditiones numerauit conuersione precantium ad Orientē πρὸς ἀνατολὰς τῆς ἡλίου ... II. Nos agnoscimus signationem crucis veterem esse ceremoniam, quae ab ipsis pene religionis Ecclesiaeq; Christianę incunabulis fuit vsurpata, sed non superstitioso modo, quo à Pontificiis, qui effectus supernaturales signo huic tribuunt, eoq; diuina veneratione crucem prosequuntur: sed vt Christiani, qui tum inter Ethnicos à Christi religione alienissimos viuebant, se Christi crucifixi cultores & adoratores esse testarentur publicè.

page.notes: Printed text is faint and partly damaged at the left edge; several initial letters are obscured by show-through and blotches. The Greek phrase after "Orientē" and the line ending "ἡλίου" are only partly legible and are transcribed approximately. The marginal notes on the left are illegible in the scan and are not transcribed. Words such as "tur" and "Ethnicos" may carry doubtful letters.
